title: Sprint Retrospective — Team Phoenix
description: Sprint 14 retro: what went well, what didn't, what we'll change.
transcript: 00:03 Arjun Mehta: Welcome to the Sprint 14 retro, everyone. Same format as always — what went well, what didn't, and what we'll change. Brutal honesty is welcome and, uh, encouraged.
00:19 Priya Sharma: Can we start with the wins? I think we need to hear those first this sprint.
00:26 Arjun Mehta: Agreed. Wins first.
00:29 Priya Sharma: The design system migration finished two days early. We converted 40 components with only three regressions, and all three were fixed the same day.
00:44 Diya Patel: The CI pipeline update was a huge win too. Build times went from 14 minutes down to 4, which basically gave everyone back an hour a day.
00:58 Rahul Verma: I'll add one — the on-call rotation change. Nobody got paged more than twice this sprint. Last sprint I got paged nine times in one week, which was honestly brutal.
01:14 Arjun Mehta: Those are three genuinely great wins. Anything else before we move to the hard part?
01:20 Sneha Rao: Small thing, but the research summaries you all started putting in the channel — really helpful. Keep doing that.
01:29 Arjun Mehta: Noted, we'll keep it up. Okay — what didn't go well? Who's brave?
01:37 Rahul Verma: I'll go. The migration backfill was a disaster. We scoped it at eight hours and it took closer to thirty. We hit row-count limits we should have known about in advance.
01:53 Arjun Mehta: Why didn't we catch that in planning? Was it unknown or just unlooked?
02:00 Rahul Verma: Honestly, a bit of both. We never load-tested against the legacy dataset, and the dataset is ten times bigger than what we designed for.
02:13 Arjun Mehta: So the lesson is we size migration work against real data volumes, not estimated ones. Can we make that a planning checklist item?
02:23 Diya Patel: I can add it to the planning template — a mandatory data-volume check for any migration ticket.
02:30 Arjun Mehta: Please do. Next — anything else that hurt?
02:35 Priya Sharma: The handoff between design and engineering broke down mid-sprint. We had three days where engineering built from outdated Figma files because the version links weren't updated.
02:51 Arjun Mehta: How do we prevent that? Is this a tooling problem or a process problem?
02:57 Priya Sharma: A bit of both, but I think a single source-of-truth link in the ticket would solve 90% of it.
03:05 Arjun Mehta: Let's do that — every design ticket gets a canonical Figma link in the description. I'll own updating the ticket template.
03:16 Diya Patel: One more from me — the incident on the 12th. The caching outage took 40 minutes to diagnose because our runbook was out of date.
03:29 Arjun Mehta: That one's on all of us. The runbook hadn't been touched since April.
03:35 Rahul Verma: We could do a runbook review day — once a sprint, two hours, we all review one service's runbook together.
03:45 Arjun Mehta: I like that. Rotating ownership, one service per sprint. Who wants to own the first one?
03:52 Rahul Verma: I'll take the first — the caching service, obviously, since it just burned us.
03:59 Arjun Mehta: Perfect. Okay, let's also do a quick temperature check — how's morale, honestly? One word each?
04:09 Priya Sharma: Optimistic.
04:12 Diya Patel: Tired, but good tired.
04:16 Rahul Verma: Recovering. This sprint was much better than the last.
04:22 Sneha Rao: Energized — the research velocity is finally picking up.
04:28 Arjun Mehta: Mine is grateful. This team handled a rough sprint without pointing fingers, and that's rare. Okay — action items. Let me read them back and confirm owners.
04:41 Arjun Mehta: Diya adds the data-volume check to the planning template. Diya, by next sprint planning?
04:49 Diya Patel: Yes, I'll have it in the template before planning on Monday.
04:53 Arjun Mehta: I update the ticket template with the canonical Figma link. That's on me by Wednesday.
05:00 Arjun Mehta: Rahul runs the first runbook review on the caching service. When?
05:06 Rahul Verma: Let's say the 28th, two hours, whole team invited.
05:12 Arjun Mehta: And one carryover — the backfill. Rahul, where does it stand?
05:18 Rahul Verma: Fixed as of yesterday, finally. The batching approach worked. Zero data loss, verified counts.
05:27 Arjun Mehta: Good. Last one — I'll take sharing these retro outcomes with the stakeholders in the weekly update by Friday. Anything I missed?
05:38 Sneha Rao: One small ask — can the design handoff fix also include a comment from design when something changes? Not just the link.
05:47 Priya Sharma: Yes, I'll add a change-note convention to the design system docs by Thursday.
05:55 Arjun Mehta: All right, that's the retro. Great sprint recovery, everyone. Thanks!
06:03 Diya Patel: Thanks all!

summary.overview: Sprint 14 retrospective. Wins: the design system migration finished two days early (40 components, 3 same-day-fixed regressions), CI build times dropped from 14 to 4 minutes, and the on-call rotation change reduced pages (Rahul: 9/week last sprint → max 2 this sprint). Misses: the migration backfill took ~30 hours against an 8-hour estimate (real data volumes 10× the design assumption), design-engineering handoff broke down over outdated Figma links (3 lost days), and the September 12th caching outage took 40 minutes to diagnose due to a stale runbook. Agreements: data-volume checks in planning, canonical Figma links in tickets, rotating runbook reviews. Morale: recovering and optimistic.

Agreements: data-volume check in planning template, canonical Figma link per ticket, rotating 2-hour runbook reviews
Morale check: optimistic, tired-but-good, recovering, energized, grateful

comments.body: Three straight sprints of build-time improvement — worth celebrating in the all-hands.
The planning checklist change should prevent this whole class of mis-estimates.
